subject.title: fix: Windows /restart falls back to in-process restart without changing PID

question: Should env-less Windows gateways with an installed Scheduled Task be treated as supervised by probing `schtasks`, or should `/restart` keep same-process fallback semantics unless service markers are present?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but changing supervisor detection affects restart availability and custom/profile task behavior, so the permanent Windows restart contract needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Probe The Matching Scheduled Task
options.body: Adopt the linked PR direction after it resolves the exact task-name contract and supplies redacted Windows `/restart` plus `/status` proof.

options.title: Keep Marker-Only Supervision
options.body: Leave env-missing Windows `/restart` in-process and document that users must start through the Scheduled Task for fresh-PID restarts.

options.title: Defer For Broader Restart Design
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define a larger Windows restart/recovery contract covering schtasks failures and status truth.

recommendation.title: Probe The Matching Scheduled Task
recommendation.body: Adopt the linked PR direction after it resolves the exact task-name contract and supplies redacted Windows `/restart` plus `/status` proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Windows Scheduled Task restart path and are the clearest history-backed owner for the supervisor detection contract.
